A.explanation: This would close only a $10 \text{m}$ gap in $1.0 \text{s}$, not the $50 \text{m}$ separation shown.

B.explanation: This uses $50 \text{m}$ divided by $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$, which ignores that Y is also moving forward at $20 \text{m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: This uses $50 \text{m}$ divided by $20 \text{m s}^{-1}$, which is the time for Y alone to travel $50 \text{m}$, not the time to close the gap.

D.explanation: The gap closes at $30 - 20 = 10 \text{m s}^{-1}$, so $50 \text{m}$ is closed in $5.0 \text{s}$.

hints: Notice from the diagram that X starts $50 \text{m}$ behind Y and both travel in the same direction at constant velocity.
Connect the two velocities $30 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $20 \text{m s}^{-1}$ to the rate at which the separation shrinks using relative velocity.
Divide the initial $50 \text{m}$ separation by the closing speed to find the time $t$ when their displacements become equal.
walkthrough: Take X starting position as zero, so at time $t$ displacement of X is $s_X = 30t$ and displacement of Y is $s_Y = 50 + 20t$, with distances in $\text{m}$ and $t$ in $\text{s}$.
For constant velocity use $s = vt$, and for X to be level with Y their displacements must be equal, so $30t = 50 + 20t$.
Alternatively use relative motion: X gains on Y at $30 - 20 = 10 \text{m s}^{-1}$ and must gain $50 \text{m}$.
Hence $t = 50/10 = 5.0 \text{s}$ with correct units of $\text{s}$. This is option D.
